parityBaseline.head: 8410a74
parityBaseline.what: One panel, three modes (signIn | signUp | forgotPassword), two steps each (details -> code), plus a done confirmation. The named render this case is ported from.

workItems.ownerBoundary: UNCHANGED. It already owns the sign-in reading order and its six states, and it is already wired to the real signIn mutation. This item exists in the matrix so the case records that it is deliberately untouched rather than forgotten.

stateInventory.evidence: rendered and wired; signIn returns a session or a two-factor challenge
the panel's own state for an account that owes TOTP
the link journey becomes the code journey; this state's successor lives in page-forgot-password
the OAuth round trip; still not completable in this build

workItems.ownerBoundary: The second step of BOTH new journeys: the code entry, the expiry sentence, the resend control and its cooldown, and the way back to the first step. It knows what a code MEANS; it does not know which journey it is finishing.

stateInventory.evidence: signUpInit and forgotPasswordInit both answer with a challenge and a TTL
OTP_CODE_INVALID_EXCEPTION, proven in the e2e; the challenge survives so the reader retypes
OTP_RESEND_TOO_SOON_EXCEPTION; the sixty seconds are real and the control must say so
OTP_CHALLENGE_NOT_FOUND_EXCEPTION; the only way forward is to start again
one request in flight must refuse a second press

workItems.ownerBoundary: The two-step account creation and which step is showing. The panel owns what is asked; the OTP block owns the second step.

stateInventory.evidence: signUpInit takes email, password and an optional name
@MinLength(8) on the input; a weak password never reaches the challenge
signUpVerifyOtp returns a session and sets the refresh cookie
createUser throws on a 409 - and it throws at VERIFY, after the code is spent, which is a journey the reader can reach

workItems.ownerBoundary: The two-step reset and which step is showing. It must not, in any state, say whether an address is registered.

stateInventory.evidence: forgotPasswordVerifyOtp takes challengeId, otp and newPassword together
the mutation answers a boolean, NOT a session - setting a password is not signing in

PROVEN INDISTINGUISHABLE rather than absent: the e2e asserts an unknown address returns the same flag, sentence, TTL and mail as a known one, and the refusal only arrives after the code is proved, wearing the same words an expired challenge wears. A state here would be the leak.

evidence.claim: signUpInit, signUpResend, signUpVerifyOtp, signInInit, signInResend, signInVerifyOtp, forgotPasswordInit, forgotPasswordResend, forgotPasswordVerifyOtp all resolve.
25 passing assertions across the three journeys, including the refusals: wrong code, replay, cooldown, unknown challenge, weak password.
an unknown address answers identically to a known one - same success flag, message, TTL and mailed code.
SignInPanel ships six states and SignInPage is wired to the real signIn mutation, with a session provider above it.
the reference panel carries rememberMe, agreeToTerms and openLegal - and starci's own src/app has no terms or privacy route, so those links resolve to nothing there either.
the refresh cookie's maxAge is a fixed 30 days with no per-request control, so a remember-me switch has nothing to switch.

unknowns: Whether sign-up should collect a display name. signUpInit accepts an optional `name`; the reference form does not ask for one.
What the sign-up journey does when the address is already registered. createUser throws at VERIFY - after the code has been spent - so the reader has proved an inbox and still cannot proceed.
Whether the OAuth shortcuts belong on the sign-up panel as well as sign-in. exchangeOauthCode is one mutation for both, but this build completes neither.
Whether the shipped `resetLinkSent` state is removed once the code journey lands, or kept for accounts created before it.

directions.thesis: Port the reference panel whole: one card, three modes switched in place, two steps each. Cut only what nivo has no mechanism to support, and name every cut.
directions.primaryCta: Tiếp tục - one button that means the next step, whichever mode is showing
tradeoffs: Replaces SignInPanel, a block that is already approved, already wired and already rendering.
The TOTP hole is patched with a third step the reference has no state for, so the closest-to-parity direction still diverges where it matters most.
Remember-me and the terms checkbox are cut, and would have to return if nivo ever grows the mechanisms behind them.
legacyDivergence: No remember-me: the refresh cookie's lifetime is fixed.
No terms checkbox: there is no page to link to, in either repository.
A third step for TOTP, which the reference does not have.

directions.primaryCta: Đăng nhập on the existing panel; Tiếp tục on each new one
tradeoffs: Not the reference's topology: three routes rather than one card that switches. Pressing 'Tạo tài khoản' navigates rather than swapping in place.
Three panels sharing one grammar are three places that grammar can drift.
signInInit and signInVerifyOtp, just built and tested, go unused on the sign-in path.
legacyDivergence: Mode switching is navigation rather than in-place state.
No remember-me and no terms checkbox, for the same absent mechanisms as direction-a.

directions.thesis: If every sign-in has to open an inbox anyway, the password field is a step in front of the real step. Sign in with an email and a code; the password survives for sign-up and for the direct path.
directions.primaryCta: Xác nhận on the code step
tradeoffs: signInInit REQUIRES a password today and grants it before mailing - that grant is what stops the endpoint mailing strangers on demand. Removing the password removes the shield, and nothing existing replaces it.
A reader cannot sign in while mail is slow or filtered, and that is every time rather than once.
legacyDivergence: The sign-in mode asks for no password at all, which the reference does not do.

backendEnablerProposals.status: REQUIRED, and it is a defect rather than a feature
backendEnablerProposals.uiNeed: none - this direction does not use the OTP sign-in path at all
backendEnablerProposals.evidence: signInVerifyOtp returns requiresTwoFactor: false unconditionally, while signIn gates on user.twoFactorEnabled and issues a challenge. An account with TOTP enabled can therefore sign in through the OTP path without its second factor.
backendEnablerProposals.escalationTrigger: Selecting direction-b means nothing in this app calls that path today - which fixes the exposure by not using it, and does NOT fix the hole. The mutation is in the live schema and anything else that calls it inherits the bypass.

backendEnablerProposals.uiNeed: a test that proves a resend actually delivers a new code
backendEnablerProposals.evidence: OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_MS is 60s and OtpChallengeService reads the wall clock, so no flow can reach the successful resend without sleeping a minute.
backendEnablerProposals.escalationTrigger: the resend control is drawn in the UI and its happy path has never been executed by a test
